title: How to Style Pillows on a Couch: Sizes & Arrangements
h1: How to Style Pillows on a Couch: Sizes, Numbers and Arrangements That Work
description: Learn how to style pillows on a couch: how many to use, a pillow size guide by sofa length, named arrangements to copy and how to mix colors and patterns.

key_takeaways: Most 72 to 90 in. sofas look best with four or five pillows; loveseats with two or three.
Use 20 to 22 in. squares on a standard sofa and keep the largest pillow below the top of the back cushion.
Copy a named arrangement: 2+2 symmetric, 3+2, asymmetric 3+1, simple pair or lumbar-only.
Mix a solid, a small pattern and a large pattern within a three-color palette, and vary textures.
Buy inserts 2 in. larger than the cover so pillows look full and keep their shape.

faq.q: How many throw pillows should be on a couch?
faq.a: A standard 3-seat sofa of 72 to 90 inches usually looks best with four or five pillows. A loveseat needs two or three, a large sofa five or six, and a sectional five to nine depending on its size. Odd numbers feel relaxed and collected, while even numbers feel formal and symmetrical.

faq.q: What size throw pillows are best for a sofa?
faq.a: For most modern sofas, 20 or 22 inch square pillows work as the main pair, with 18 to 20 inch squares or a 14 by 24 inch lumbar in front. Loveseats suit 18 to 20 inch squares, while deep or large sofas and sectionals can take 24 inch squares. The largest pillow should sit a few inches below the top of the back cushion.

faq.q: How do you arrange 5 pillows on a couch?
faq.a: Place two matching large squares at each end, set two slightly smaller pillows in front of them, then add one lumbar or contrasting square in the center. This 3+2 arrangement suits sofas of 84 to 100 inches. Make the center pillow your boldest pattern or richest texture so it becomes the focal point.

faq.q: How do you mix and match throw pillows?
faq.a: Pick a three-color palette drawn from your sofa, rug and art. Then combine a solid, a small-scale pattern and a large-scale pattern so the prints do not compete. Add variety in texture with linen, velvet, bouclé or knit. Keep the patterns linked by at least one shared color.

faq.q: Should throw pillows match the couch?
faq.a: No. Pillows should contrast with the sofa so they stand out. Use darker or richer textures on a light sofa and lighter fabrics such as linen or bouclé on a dark sofa. A pillow in exactly the same fabric as the upholstery tends to disappear. Repeat pillow colors elsewhere in the room instead.
